newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Relief over Lonrho/JCI abandonment.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Relief over Lonrho/JCI abandonment.

text.p: British conglomerate Lonrho Plc abandoned talks on merging its mining interests with South Africa's JCI Ltd on Monday, a decision met with relief by London analysts, despite a slight drop in the group's share price.

The UK-based mining, hotels and trading group said in a brief statement it had discontinued talks with black-controlled JCI to form a mining company worth around $3 billion, although it did not give any reasons.

Shares in Lonrho were down 2 1/2 pence to 129 in late morning trading in London, recovering from an initial drop of five pence per share. In South Africa the reaction was sharper, with Lonrho shares dropping more than four percent at one stage. Shares in JCI slid 50 cents to 25 rand.
JCI in Johannesburg said it was discussing other ways to unlock value for shareholders in both JCI and Lonrho after the merger talks were called off.

"JCI Ltd announces that it has discontinued talks with Lonrho Plc about a possible merger. However, the company confirms that it has been approached to discuss other possible transactions which could unlock value for shareholders in both JCI Ltd and Lonrho," JCI said.
It gave no further details in a brief statement.
The companies said last month they were in preliminary talks, but reports last week said prospects of the merger going through were fading.
However analysts in London said any merger with JCI would have been premature, with Lonrho still struggling to reorganise itself and dispose of its non-core hotel and African trading operations.
Paribas analyst Charles Kernot said the merger did not make sense. "It would have been a very backward step for both Lonrho and JCI," he added.
Lonrho is still working on plans to demerge its African trading operations. Although the company expects this to be well underway by the end of the year, a number of uncertainties remain.
The company is also keen to complete the sale of its Princess hotels chain.

Analysts said merger talks may have been intended to help JCI to push up the value of its own shares, which have fallen sharply since it was formed last year by South Africa's Anglo American mining group.

Failure of the negotiations between JCI and Lonrho will boost speculation about other potential tie-ups between Lonrho's mining operations and other south African groups, including Anglo American and Gencor, analysts said.
Paribas's Kernot said a link with South Africa's Gencor would be quite a good fit. That is one to look at."

Last week, Lonrho's founder Tiny Rowland, who is still the group's largest individual shareholder despite being ousted from the company, launched a scathing attack on the proposed merger with JCI, accusing Anglo American of driving the deal in its own interests.
